subject.title: fix(codex): clean final/yield turn close writes a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout

question: Should explicit Codex terminal delivery wait up to 10 seconds for natural `turn/completed`, with immediate interrupt only for new inbound work or a runaway deadline, instead of preserving the current immediate-interrupt behavior?
rationale: Both paths deliberately trade rollout integrity, completion latency, and treatment of post-final work; the code cannot determine the intended product semantics.

options.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
options.body: Keep the 10-second absolute deadline and immediate new-inbound fallback so normal explicit-final closes avoid writing a false user-interrupt marker.

options.title: Keep immediate interruption
options.body: Retain the existing hard-stop behavior and accept the Codex rollout marker in exchange for immediate attempt resolution.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Keep the natural-completion architecture but change the deadline or new-inbound behavior before merge.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
recommendation.body: Keep the 10-second absolute deadline and immediate new-inbound fallback so normal explicit-final closes avoid writing a false user-interrupt marker.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged continuation/finalization work is the closest current-main owner of the terminal source-reply behavior this policy extends.
